questions.stem: An adult drank antifreeze. Which antidote blocks it from turning toxic?
questions.explanation: C is correct: fomepizole stops toxic alcohols turning into toxic acids. A reverses opioids. B treats iron. D treats beta blockers.

questions.stem: After a single acute acetaminophen overdose, when should the level be drawn to plot on the chart?
questions.explanation: A is correct: draw a level between 4 and 24 hours. B and D are before 4 hours, which cannot be plotted. C is outside the chart.

questions.stem: After a single overdose, the acetaminophen level is 180 at 4 hours. What is the next step?
questions.explanation: D is correct: the level is above the treatment line, which starts at 150 at 4 hours, so start acetylcysteine. A delays treatment. B is not enough. C treats toxic alcohols.

questions.stem: Match the poison to its antidote. Which pairs are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, D, and E are correct as taught. C is wrong because cyanide gets hydroxocobalamin.

questions.stem: A toddler ate a bottle of iron pills. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Give deferoxamine; charcoal does not bind iron

questions.explanation: B is correct: deferoxamine is the antidote, and activated charcoal does not bind iron. A is wrong. C reverses opioids. D treats toxic alcohols.

questions.stem: Match the heart drug overdose to its treatment. Which pairs are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Calcium channel blockers: intravenous calcium and high-dose insulin

questions.explanation: A, B, C, and D are correct as taught. E is wrong because protamine reverses heparin.

questions.stem: Which finding points to anticholinergic poisoning?

options.text: Wide pupils with hot, dry, red skin and confusion

questions.explanation: B is correct: anticholinergic drugs cause wide pupils, with hot, dry, red skin and confusion. A fits opioids. C and D fit organophosphates.

questions.stem: A farm worker is drooling and sweating, with pinpoint pupils and a slow heart. What is the best treatment?
questions.explanation: B is correct: wet, slow, and pinpoint points to organophosphate poisoning, treated with atropine plus pralidoxime. A reverses opioids. C is for select anticholinergic cases. D reverses benzodiazepines and can trigger seizures.
B is correct: flumazenil can trigger seizures. A is not the reason given. C is wrong because naloxone is the opioid antidote. D is not a flumazenil effect.

questions.stem: Which statements about activated charcoal are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: It is the antidote for antifreeze
It works best within an hour

questions.explanation: C, D, and E are correct as taught. A is wrong because antifreeze gets fomepizole. B is wrong because naloxone reverses opioids.
